title: Nehemiah's Prayer and Commission
summary: Nehemiah, cupbearer to Artaxerxes at Shushan, hears from his brother Hanani that Jerusalem's wall is broken and its gates burned. He weeps, fasts and prays, confessing Israel's sins and asking for favor. Four months later, when the king notices his sad face, Nehemiah prays quickly and asks to be sent to rebuild; the king grants letters of passage and timber for the gates. Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite are displeased that someone has come to seek Israel's good.

title: Rebuilding the Wall
summary: After three days in Jerusalem Nehemiah inspects the wall by night and persuades the leaders to rebuild; priests, families and guilds take sections. Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem mock and plot an attack. Nehemiah posts guards and arms half the workers with spears while the other half builds, with a trumpeter at his side, and tells the people, 'Our God shall fight for us.' Workers carry weapons even at night, and no one takes off his clothes except for washing.

title: Debt Relief
summary: A cry goes up from poor families who mortgage fields and vineyards and sell children to pay taxes and buy grain during a famine. Nehemiah, angered, calls a great assembly and rebukes the nobles and rulers for charging interest from their kinsmen. They agree to return the property and the interest, and Nehemiah makes them swear oaths before the priests. He adds that during his twelve years as governor he did not take the governor's food allowance and lent freely.

title: The Wall Completed
summary: Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem try four times to lure Nehemiah to a meeting on the plain of Ono, and Nehemiah answers that he is doing a great work and cannot come down. They then send an open letter accusing him of planning rebellion, and hire Shemaiah to scare him into the temple; Nehemiah refuses. The wall is finished in fifty-two days, and the neighboring nations lose confidence. Nehemiah puts Hanani and Hananiah in charge of Jerusalem and finds a register of those who first returned.

title: Ezra Reads the Law
summary: On the first day of the seventh month all the people gather at the water gate, and Ezra reads the law from morning to midday while the Levites explain it. The people weep, but Nehemiah and Ezra tell them to rejoice, for the joy of the LORD is their strength. They find the command about booths and keep the Feast of Tabernacles. Two days after the feast, they fast in sackcloth, confess their sins, and hear a long prayer recounting God's dealings with Israel from creation to the present.

title: The Covenant and Dedication of the Wall
summary: The leaders, Levites and priests sign a covenant to walk in God's law, avoid intermarriage with the surrounding peoples, keep the Sabbath, and support the temple with offerings, firstfruits and tithes. One in ten of the people is chosen by lot to live in Jerusalem, and the chapters list the settlements, priests and Levites. At the wall's dedication, two great companies give thanks, walking in opposite directions on the wall and meeting at the temple.

title: Nehemiah's Reforms
summary: After a trip to the Persian king, Nehemiah returns to find that the priest Eliashib has given Tobiah a large room in the temple, and he throws out Tobiah's belongings and has the rooms cleansed. He finds the Levites unpaid and gone to their fields, and restores the tithes. When merchants trade on the Sabbath, he shuts the gates at dusk and threatens the traders. He also rebukes Jews who married foreign wives, and ends with a prayer, 'Remember me, O my God, for good.'
